activities.name: Luncheon in Stresa
activities.location: Grand Hotel des Iles Borromées, Corso Umberto I, 67, 28838 Stresa VB, Italy
activities.notes: Enjoy lunch at the Grand Hotel des Iles Borromées, a luxurious Belle Époque landmark on Lake Maggiore. Ernest Hemingway stayed here in 1918 while recovering from war wounds, later immortalizing it in his novel 'A Farewell to Arms.' Winston Churchill also visited the hotel, drawn by its grandeur and lakeside tranquility. The historic setting offers exquisite cuisine and panoramic lake views that have inspired generations of statesmen, artists, and writers.

activities.name: Visit Isola Bella
activities.location: Isola Bella, Lake Maggiore, 28838 Stresa VB, Italy
activities.notes: Isola Bella, named for Isabella, Countess Borromeo, was originally a barren rock. After initial developments by Count Carlo III (1629–1652), his son Vitaliano VI transformed it into a lavish summer palace, importing vast amounts of soil to create ten elaborate terraced gardens. The palace contains Lombard paintings and Flemish tapestries. Napoleon and Joséphine Bonaparte visited in 1797 and were guests of the Borromeo family, impressed by the grandeur. In the 20th century, Benito Mussolini met with foreign ministers on the island in 1935 during the Stresa Conference, which attempted to reaffirm European unity in the face of rising tensions. These layers of political and artistic history make Isola Bella a cultural landmark as well as a visual marvel.

activities.name: Dinner at Veranda
activities.notes: Lakeside dining at the hotel. DRESS CODE: Jackets, long trousers, and closed shoes are required for gentlemen at dinner. Located in the Cardinal’s Building, the fine-dining Veranda restaurant offers glorious views of the lake, gardens and Mosaic. The retractable windows remain open throughout the summer and, weather permitting, diners can savour dinner on the lakeside terrace. Classic and contemporary Italian cuisine is ennobled with international touches. Executive Chef Michele Zambanini blends ceaseless research and the finest ingredients with the utmost respect for seasonal produce. In this formal, elegant setting, guests experience haute cuisine alongside a curated wine selection, in addition to professional service tailored to the desires of every guest.

activities.name: Night Cap at Canova Bar and Lake Terrace
activities.notes: The Canova Bar has been regarded as the most glamorous place to sip a cocktail on Lake Como since 1873. The sumptuous interior make the bar an exclusive spot to people-watch and to be seen at any time of day. Throughout the summer, guests are invited to sit alfresco on the lake terrace, beneath majestic chestnut trees and surrounded by the scent of jasmine.

activities.name: 8 Hour Private Boat Tour of the Lake
activities.notes:
Vaporinas were the first motorboats to be created on Lake Como in the late 1800s.
Elongated with a sleek design, the roof was originally partly covered in glass. Naval
architect Carlo Bertorello worked with yacht manufacturer extraordinaire Cantiere Riva to
modernize this charming boat, adding comfort and technology, while upholding the
classic style. It’s definitely worth a ride!

activities.name: Lunch at Da Giacomo al Lago at the Grand Hotel Tremezzo
activities.notes: In the 1930s, Greta Garbo, Alfred Hitchcock, and Frank Sinatra made the location famous for not just vacations, but as a scenic setting for movies of all genres. Today, celebrities and dignitaries alike flock to the shores of Lake Como, recognizing its beautiful treasured waters.

activities.name: Explore Bellagio and enjoy a quick drink at Alle Darsene di Loppia
activities.notes: Begin with a walk through Bellagio’s scenic village—boutique shops, cobblestone lanes, and panoramic lake views from the peninsula tip. Wrap up with a quick drink at Alle Darsene di Loppia, a charming lakeside restaurant located near the gardens of Villa Melzi. This quiet harbor spot offers a relaxing pause before continuing your journey.

activities.name: Visit Villa Melzi
activities.notes: Villa Melzi d'Eril was built between 1808 and 1810 for Francesco Melzi d'Eril, vice president of the Napoleonic Italian Republic. The neoclassical villa is surrounded by English-style botanical gardens with rare exotic plants, sculptures, and breathtaking lake views.

activities.name: Explore Varenna
activities.notes: Varenna is a picturesque lakeside town known for its narrow alleyways, colorful houses, and romantic atmosphere. Stroll along the 'Passeggiata degli Innamorati' (Lovers’ Walk) and stop for a coffee at Il Bar al Molo, a cozy café with waterside views near the ferry dock.

activities.name: Visit Villa Monastero
activities.location: Via Giovanni Polvani, 4, 23829 Varenna LC, Italy
activities.notes: Originally a 12th-century Cistercian convent, Villa Monastero was transformed into a noble residence and is now a museum and conference center. The villa boasts eclectic interiors and extensive botanical gardens stretching nearly 2 kilometers along the lake.

activities.name: Dinner at Il Gatto Nero Amy and Chet
activities.location: Via Della Liberta', 69, 22012 Cernobbio CO, Italy

Ideal for romantic encounters, as well as business and group dinners. The Gatto Nero restaurant is a popular destination for visiting celebrities, including George Clooney and other well-known Hollywood stars, Italian and international politicians, world-famous sportsmen and women, in addition to a large, local clientele.

Opened in 1891 by Emperor Franz Joseph I, the Kunsthistorisches Museum is one of the most important art museums in the world, housing works by masters such as Bruegel, Caravaggio, and Velázquez in a grand neo-Renaissance palace.

This stand near the Albertina is one of Vienna’s most iconic, known for elevating sausage culture with flair and quality since the early 2000s.

activities.name: Dessert at Hotel Sacher
activities.notes: We have 12:45 reservation at Café Sacher Wien. The coffee, hot chocolate and Sacher-Torte, a chocolate cake, are legendary. The original Sacher-Torte was created in 1832 by Franz Sacher for Prince Metternich and has become one of Austria’s most famous culinary creations.

activities.name: Meet Guide at Hotel Lobby and Walk to Hohensalzburg
Private Tour of Salzburg Fortress (Hohensalzburg)
activities.notes: Opens at 8:30 AM 7 days a week. Funicular ride up and tour of medieval fortress. The Hohensalzburg Fortress, perched atop the Festungsberg hill, is one of the largest and best-preserved medieval castles in Europe. Construction began in 1077 under Archbishop Gebhard during a period of conflict between the Pope and the Holy Roman Emperor. Over centuries, it was expanded into a mighty bastion of ecclesiastical power, symbolizing the independence and influence of the Prince-Archbishops of Salzburg. It was never conquered by foreign troops and offers panoramic views of the city and Alps.

activities.name: Walk to Salzburg Cathedral
activities.notes: Scenic walk through Salzburg’s Old Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, rich with baroque architecture and historic charm.

activities.name: DomQuartier and Salzburg Cathedral
activities.notes: Tour the DomQuartier, a baroque museum complex that includes the Salzburg Cathedral, the Residenz Palace, and the Cathedral Museum. In The Temptation of St Anthony (c 1500) an imaginative follower of Hieronymus Bosch depicts hell encroaching upon earth. Highlights include state rooms with elaborate ceiling frescoes, a view into the cathedral nave from the organ loft, and rare religious art. This complex captures the grandeur of Salzburg’s ecclesiastical past under the Prince-Archbishops. The Salzburg Cathedral itself was consecrated in 1628 and is renowned for its monumental baroque façade, twin towers, and the baptismal font in which Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was baptized.

activities.name: Lunch at Meissl & Schadn
activities.notes: Customize your Wiener schnitzel at Meissl & Schadn, where you can choose from clarified butter, lard, or vegetable oil. Side dishes are taken seriously: try the parsley potatoes, cucumber salad, or the classic 'Wiener Garnitur' (chopped egg, capers, anchovy, and herbs). Vegetarian schnitzel made with celery root is available. For dessert or a light treat, grab a scoop from Moritz Eis across the street.

activities.name: Shnapps and Shops at Sporer and Stassny
activities.notes: Both located on either side of our hotel Sporer specializes in Shnapps and Stassny in updated traditional native fashon.

activities.name: Tour Mozart’s Birthplace and Salzburg Heimatwerk
activities.notes: Visit the apartment where Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was born in 1756, now a well-designed museum showcasing the composer’s early life and work. Notable exhibits include his childhood violin and set designs from his operas. Nearby, explore the Salzburg Heimatwerk for upscale traditional clothing and crafts. The dirndls are made to last generations, priced around €1,000, and tailored with exacting detail.

Salzburger Nockerl at Café Habakuk
activities.notes: Sample Salzburg’s signature dessert — Salzburger Nockerl — at Café Habakuk, a cozy spot on the busy Linzergasse. This fluffy, custardy soufflé arrives warm, with raspberry sauce at the bottom. The café is beloved for its house-made pastries and local charm. Expect about 20 minutes of preparation time for the Nockerl, which costs €13. It's the perfect indulgence before or after a walk through the nearby Old Town.

activities.name: Explore Steingasse and Antiquariat Weinek
activities.notes: Walk off breakfast with a stroll down the historic Steingasse, a narrow, atmospheric street dating to the 16th century. Stop into Antiquariat Weinek, a rare book shop and gallery that doubles as a café. It's a treasure trove of vintage volumes, prints, and local flair, serving coffee, craft beer, and wine. Even if you're not shopping, it's worth a peek for the ambiance and views.

activities.name: Walk to Mirabell Gardens
activities.notes: As you cross the bridge discover contemporary art installations along Salzburg's Walk of Modern Art, including Marina Abramovic’s 'Spirit of Mozart' and Brigitte Kowanz’s 'Beyond Recall'.

activities.name: Stroll through Mirabell Gardens
activities.notes: Mirabell Gardens in Salzburg is a prominent filming location for "The Sound of Music." Specifically, the "Do-Re-Mi" song sequence, where Maria and the Von Trapp children sing and dance, was filmed there. The iconic Pegasus Fountain and the steps leading to the rose garden are recognizable elements from the movie. The Pegasus Fountain is where the children dance around and Maria sings from its edge during the “Do-Re-Mi” scene. The musical steps leading up to the rose garden serve as a visual representation of the musical scale as Maria sings. At the garden’s entrance, the Greek fencing statues are featured as the children mimic their poses. Another memorable location within Mirabell Gardens is the Dwarf Garden, where the whimsical gnome statues make a charming appearance in the film.

activities.name: Luncheon and Coffee at Café Tomaselli or 220Grad Rupertinum
activities.notes: Café Tomaselli, in business since 1703, is a Salzburg institution known for its classic charm, wooden interiors, and excellent cakes. For a more modern take, 220Grad Rupertinum serves third-wave coffee in a bright, stylish space near the Museum der Moderne. Both offer great people-watching and a break from sightseeing.

activities.name: Walk to Checkpoint Charlie
activities.notes: Head southeast on Friedrichstraße for ~1.1 km. Turn left on Zimmerstraße. Checkpoint Charlie is at the intersection.

activities.name: Checkpoint Charlie
activities.notes: Checkpoint Charlie was the best-known Berlin Wall crossing point during the Cold War (1947–1991), symbolizing the division of East and West. In October 1961, it was the site of a dramatic tank standoff between American and Soviet forces after a dispute over travel rights for U.S. diplomats—one of the Cold War's most dangerous moments. Today, the nearby Checkpoint Charlie Museum (Haus am Checkpoint Charlie) documents stories of escape attempts, border history, and Cold War tensions through exhibits of photographs, artifacts, and even homemade contraptions used by defectors.

activities.name: Walk to Topography of Terror
activities.notes: Walk one block south on Wilhelmstraße. The Topography of Terror museum is on the left.

activities.name: Topography of Terror
activities.notes: An outdoor and indoor history museum located on the site of buildings which during the Nazi regime were the headquarters of the Gestapo and the SS.

activities.name: Walk to Luftwaffe Building
activities.notes: From Topography of Terror, walk northeast along Niederkirchnerstraße toward Wilhelmstraße. Turn left on Wilhelmstraße. The Luftwaffe Building (Detlev-Rohwedder-Haus) is at the corner of Leipziger Straße.

activities.name: Visit Luftwaffe Building (Detlev-Rohwedder-Haus)
activities.notes: Former Luftwaffe headquarters and later the seat of East Germany’s government. Under Soviet control the subect of all art was required to inspire communist ideals. Check out Detail from Max Lingner’s monumental mural “Aufbau der Republik” (“Building the Republic”).

activities.name: Walk to Führerbunker Site
activities.notes: From Detlev-Rohwedder-Haus, continue north on Wilhelmstraße. Turn left onto In den Ministergärten. The site of the Führerbunker is located near the corner with Gertrud-Kolmar-Straße and is marked with an informational sign.

activities.name: Luncheon
activities.location: India Club Berlin, Behrenstraße 72, 10117 Berlin, Germany
activities.notes: India Club Berlin is a refined restaurant located near Brandenburg Gate, offering upscale North Indian cuisine in an elegant colonial-inspired interior. Known for its tandoori dishes, fragrant curries, and extensive wine selection, the India Club does not serve beef or pork, maintaining authenticity to Indian culinary traditions. The restaurant is attached to the exclusive Hotel Adlon complex, and has become a favorite of diplomats, locals, and international visitors alike.

activities.name: Führerbunker Site
activities.notes: The Führerbunker was an air-raid shelter located near the Reich Chancellery in Berlin, where Adolf Hitler spent the final weeks of World War II and died.

activities.name: Walk to Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
activities.notes: Continue north on Wilhelmstraße, turn left on Behrenstraße and right onto Ebertstraße. The memorial will be on your left.

activities.name: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
activities.notes: A memorial to the Jewish victims of the Holocaust, consisting of 2,711 concrete slabs, designed by architect Peter Eisenman.

activities.name: Walk to Brandenburg Gate
activities.notes: Head north along Ebertstraße for about 300 meters. The Brandenburg Gate will be directly ahead at Pariser Platz.

activities.name: Stop at Brandenburg Gate
activities.notes: Look for bullet holes! One of Berlin’s most iconic landmarks, the neoclassical Brandenburg Gate once symbolized division and now represents unity. Originally commissioned by King Frederick William II in the late 18th century.

activities.name: S Bahn Subway and Russian Embassy FSB Headquarters
activities.notes: The FSB operates at a level of opacity, brutality, and reach that places it among the most feared and criticized intelligence services globally. Its tactics — including poisonings, surveillance, torture, and suppression of dissent — have led many to describe it as not just “messed up” but a critical instrument of authoritarian control in modern Russia.

activities.name: Walk to Reichstag
activities.notes: From Brandenburg Gate, continue north on Ebertstraße for another 300 meters. The Reichstag Building will be on your left.

activities.name: Tour of Reichstag
activities.notes: #SYS-20250709-111808. The Reichstag is one of the most iconic buildings in Berlin and a symbol of German democracy. Constructed between 1884 and 1894 by architect Paul Wallot, it originally housed the Imperial Diet (Reichstag) of the German Empire. It remained the seat of parliament through the Weimar Republic but lost significance under Nazi rule. In 1933, it was severely damaged by a fire—an event the Nazis used to justify a crackdown on civil liberties and consolidate power. Near the end of World War II, the Reichstag became the site of the Nazi regime’s last stand in Berlin; Soviet forces captured it during the Battle of Berlin in April 1945, famously raising their flag atop its ruins. After the war, the building sat in ruins near the Berlin Wall, symbolically divided between East and West, and was used only for occasional symbolic events in West Germany.

activities.name: Walk to Humboldt University
activities.notes: We Debark at Am Lustgarten. On the walk back we can see the statue of Frederick the Great and the Apmpleman store on Frederick street. Humboldt University, founded in 1810 by Wilhelm von Humboldt, is one of Berlin's oldest and most prestigious universities. It pioneered the modern research university model. Karl Marx studied philosophy here in the 1830s; Vladimir Lenin researched in the library in 1895; and Albert Einstein was a professor from 1914 to 1933. Located across from Bebelplatz, it remains a hub of academic excellence. It is also where the Nazi's burned the books of their library.

activities.name: Walk to Bauhaus Museum Weimar
activities.location: Walk northeast from Weimar Hauptbahnhof via Carl-August-Allee to Stéphane-Hessel-Platz.
activities.notes: Direct walk toward Weimar’s modern design legacy.

activities.name: Visit the Bauhaus Museum Weimar
activities.notes: Opening hours: 9:30 AM – 6:00 PM. The Bauhaus was founded by architect Walter Gropius in Weimar. It became one of the most influential movements in modern design and architecture. The museum holds over 13,000 objects related to Bauhaus history.

activities.name: Walk to Luncheon at AnnA, Hotel Elephant
Luncheon at AnnA, Hotel Elephant
activities.location: Hotel Elephant Weimar, Markt 19, 99423 Weimar, Germany
activities.notes: Upscale regional German cuisine served in a historic hotel on the Markt square. The hotel hosted literary figures like Goethe and Thomas Mann, and political leaders including Hitler held speeches from its balcony during the Nazi era.

activities.name: Walk to Franz Liszt House
activities.location: Walk southeast along Frauentorstraße and Marienstraße.

activities.name: Visit the House of Franz Liszt
activities.notes: Opening hours: 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM. The Liszt House was built as the court gardener’s residence. Composer Franz Liszt lived here from 1869 and held public musical salons. The museum preserves his living quarters and musical instruments.

activities.name: Walk to Anna Amalia Library
activities.location: Walk via Puschkinstraße and Platz der Demokratie.

activities.name: Visit the Rococo Hall in Anna Amalia Library
activities.notes: Opening hours: 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM. Famous for its Rococo Hall and literary archives, the library is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Founded in 1691, it became renowned under Duchess Anna Amalia in the 18th century and contains over a million volumes.

activities.name: Walk to Goethe House
activities.location: Walk southwest via Goetheplatz and Frauenplan.

activities.name: Visit the Goethe House
activities.notes: Opening hours: 9:30 AM – 6:00 PM. Historic residence of Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, now a museum chronicling his life and works. Goethe lived here for nearly 50 years and received many European intellectuals during the Enlightenment.

activities.name: Dinner at Café-Restaurant ANNO 1900
activities.notes: Classic German cuisine in a cozy vintage atmosphere. Recommended to dine between 5:30–6:30 PM. The name evokes the turn of the century when Weimar was a flourishing center for arts, literature, and reform.

activities.name: Visit Gemäldegalerie
activities.notes: Opens at 10 AM. The Gemäldegalerie houses one of the world's finest collections of European painting from the 13th to the 18th century, including masterpieces by Botticelli, Caravaggio, Rembrandt, and Vermeer. Situated adjacent to the Kupferstichkabinett in the Kulturforum.

activities.name: Visit Kupferstichkabinett
activities.notes: The Kupferstichkabinett (Museum of Prints and Drawings) holds one of the most important collections of graphic art in the world, featuring works by Albrecht Dürer, Botticelli, Rembrandt, and Picasso. Located in the Kulturforum complex.

activities.name: Luncheon and Shopping at Kunstmarkt an der Museumsinsel

activities.name: Tour of Museum Island
activities.notes: Museum Island is a UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring five internationally significant museums. Tour includes the Pergamon, Neues Museum, and Altes Museum with a guide.

activities.name: Walk to DDR Museum
activities.notes: Walk east from Museum Island along the Spree River promenade. The DDR Museum is just past the Berliner Dom.

activities.name: Visit DDR Museum
activities.notes: The DDR Museum offers an interactive experience of life in former East Germany, featuring recreated apartments, surveillance technology, and propaganda exhibits. Open daily 9:00–21:00.

activities.name: Drive to Alexanderplatz
activities.notes: Large public square and transport hub. Notable landmarks include the World Time Clock and the TV Tower (Fernsehturm).

activities.name: Drive Karl-Marx-Allee
activities.notes: Monumental socialist boulevard lined with Stalinist architecture. Originally named Stalinallee, it was the showcase of GDR urban planning.

activities.name: Visit East Side Gallery
activities.notes: The longest remaining stretch of the Berlin Wall, now an open-air gallery covered in murals by artists from around the world.
